title: Ad-hoc regulatory dossier builder with redactable summaries and signed-manifest templates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers (security and legal teams) need a way to produce ad-hoc regulatory dossiers that contain tenant-scoped evidence (logs, export snapshots, signed manifests) and human-friendly executive summaries. These dossiers must support redaction templates (PII removal/partial masking), selectable residency-scoped content (EU-only, US-only), and produce both PDF and CSV artifacts with an accompanying verifiable manifest (signed/hashed).

Goal: Build a toolkit inside the Console and Export API that lets operators: 1) assemble a dossier from saved evidence sets or query filters; 2) apply one of several redaction templates; 3) generate a ZIP containing a PDF dossier, one or more CSVs, and a machine-verifiable manifest (SHA256 + signature reference); 4) schedule recurring ad-hoc dossier deliveries (cron-style or one-off) with tenant-scoped delivery and webhook or S3 presigned link notification.

Why different from scheduled compliance exports: This ticket focuses on flexible, on-demand dossier composition with redaction templates and signed manifests for auditors, not just periodic bulk archives. It targets legal/enterprise reviewers who need readable PDFs and provable provenance alongside raw CSV evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Console: UI flow to create an Ad-hoc Dossier from saved evidence sets and from ad-hoc query; can select redaction template and residency scope
API: POST /v1/exports/dossiers accepts filters, redaction_template_id, output_formats (pdf,csv,zip), delivery (none|webhook|s3), schedule (optional crontab), and returns export_id
Redaction: At least 3 templates implemented (full-redact, pii-mask, tokenized-id) and pluggable for future custom templates
Manifest: Generated manifest.json with per-file SHA256 hashes and an export-level signed_digest pointing to customer-managed KMS key (or Redwood signing for hosted customers).
Delivery: Can schedule recurring or one-off deliveries; notifications via webhook or presigned S3 link; tenant-scoped residency routing enforced when selecting residency scope

PDF: Generated PDF includes cover page (tenant, export time, export filters), executive summary excerpt auto-generated from selected prompt set + regeneration option, and an attachments index referencing manifest entries
Audit trail: Export record stored with full provenance (creator, filters, redaction template, residency_scope, KMS_key_id if used) and visible in Console export history
Security: Exports honor RBAC and cannot be requested by users without export permission; security_review_required flagged for enterprise tenants
tasks: Spec: Draft PRD & UI mockups for console flow (owner: PM)
API: Design export request payload and validation rules (owner: Backend)
Redaction: Implement redaction engine adapters and template registry (owner: Infra/Runtime)
Provenance: Integrate SHA256 manifest generation and signing via KMS/HSM (owner: Security)
Delivery: Implement scheduler, webhook sender, and presigned S3 delivery paths (owner: Delivery)
PDF: Integrate PDF renderer with templating for cover + summary + attachments (owner: Frontend/Docs)
UI: Console pages for create, preview (redacted sample), and history (owner: Design + Frontend)
E2E: Create test harness with sample tenant data, residency flags, and QA checklist (owner: QA)
Docs: Update compliance docs and add admin guide and API examples (owner: DevRel)
comments: 2025-02-18 — Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after customer workshop with legal at Acme Corp. They required both readable PDFs for auditors and a verifiable manifest for S3-based evidence bundles.

2025-02-20 — Marco Liu: Scoped to MVP: console+API to build a dossier from saved evidence sets, add 3 redaction templates, manifest with SHA256 + Redwood signing; delivery via presigned S3 and webhook. KMS customer-managed signing deferred to follow-up but must be designed for.

2025-02-25 — Design (Jules Kim): Uploaded wireframes to Confluence: /confluence/redwood/Adhoc-Dossier-Wireframes (link). We recommend a two-step flow: filter -> preview (sample 10 rows) -> redaction preview -> schedule/deliver.

2025-02-28 — Security (Priya Nair): Flagged that signing flow requires security_review_required for enterprise tenants. Need threat model for manifest signing and key access patterns. Created GH issue: github.com/redwood-inference/security/issues/112

2025-03-01 — Backend (Diego Ramos): Prototype API endpoint schema in PR: github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/459. Key questions: max export size per tenant, on-the-fly redaction vs precomputed, job timeouts. Proposed default max rows 500k, chunked CSV streaming for large sets.

2025-03-02 — PM (Aisha Patel): Revised acceptance criteria — added explicit requirement for cover page and executive summary auto-generation using stored prompt templates; added due_date to align with enterprise demo on 2025-04-16.

2025-03-03 — Marco Liu: Planned follow-up spikes: 1) KMS integration for customer key signing (est 3 pts), 2) Redaction QA for multilingual PII (est 5 pts). Adding dependency on PM-14577 (residency routing refactor) to ensure export respects regionality.
